sanskrit: putratvaṃ tu gate viṣṇau rājñas tasya mahātmanaḥ uvāca devatāḥ sarvāḥ svayambhūr bhagavān idam
english: When Viṣṇu had entered into sonship with that great-souled king, Svayambhū — the Self-born Lord — spoke these words to all the gods:

sanskrit: satyasaṃdhasya vīrasya sarveṣāṃ no hitaiṣiṇaḥ viṣṇoḥ sahāyān balinaḥ sṛjadhvaṃ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: "For the sake of Viṣṇu — the hero who is true to his vows and who desires the welfare of us all — create mighty helpers who can take any form at will.

sanskrit: māyāvidaś ca śūrāṃś ca vāyuvegasamāñjave nayajñān buddhisaṃpannān viṣṇutulyaparākramān
english: Create warriors skilled in illusion, swift as the wind, versed in statecraft, endowed with keen intelligence, and equal to Viṣṇu in valour.

sanskrit: asaṃhāryān upāyajñān divyasaṃhananānvitān sarvāstraguṇasaṃpannān amṛtaprāśanān iva
english: Create them invincible, skilled in every stratagem, possessed of divine physiques, proficient in the use of all weapons, and as it were nourished on immortal nectar.

sanskrit: apsaraḥsu ca mukhyāsu gandharvīṇāṃ tanūṣu ca yakṣapannagakanyāsu ṛṣkavidyādharīṣu ca
english: Upon the foremost of the Apsarases, upon the bodies of Gandharvī women, upon the daughters of Yakṣas and Nāgas, upon female Ṛṣkas and Vidyādharīs,

sanskrit: kiṃnarīṇāṃ ca gātreṣu vānarīṇāṃ tanūṣu ca sṛjadhvaṃ harirūpeṇa putrāṃs tulyaparākramān
english: upon the bodies of Kiṃnarī women and upon female monkeys — beget sons in the form of monkeys, equal in valour to one another."

sanskrit: te tathoktā bhagavatā tat pratiśrutya śāsanam janayām āsur evaṃ te putrān vānararūpiṇaḥ
english: Thus instructed by the Lord, they accepted his command and accordingly begot sons in the form of monkeys.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś ca mahātmānaḥ siddhavidyādharoragāḥ cāraṇāś ca sutān vīrān sasṛjur vanacāriṇaḥ
english: The great-souled sages, the Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Nāgas, and Cāraṇas likewise begot heroic sons who roamed the forests.

sanskrit: te sṛṣṭā bahusāhasrā daśagrīvavadhodyatāḥ aprameyabalā vīrā vikrāntāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: Those created in their thousands, intent on slaying the ten-necked Rāvaṇa, were heroes of immeasurable strength, brave, vigorous, and able to assume any form at will.

sanskrit: te gajācalasaṃkāśā vapuṣmanto mahābalāḥ ṛkṣavānaragopucchāḥ kṣipram evābhijajñire
english: Resembling elephants and mountains, handsome and mighty, they were born quickly as bears, monkeys, and gopucchas.

sanskrit: yasya devasya yad rūpaṃ veṣo yaś ca parākramaḥ ajāyata samastena tasya tasya sutaḥ pṛthak
english: Whatever form, appearance, and valour belonged to each particular deity — with that entirety was each one's offspring separately born.

sanskrit: golāṅgūlīṣu cotpannāḥ ke cit saṃmatavikramāḥ ṛkṣīṣu ca tathā jātā vānarāḥ kiṃnarīṣu ca
english: Some of approved valour were born of the golāṅgūlī females; others were born of female bears and monkey-women, and yet others of Kiṃnarī women.

sanskrit: śilāpraharaṇāḥ sarve sarve pādapayodhinaḥ nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhāḥ sarve sarve sarvāstrakovidāḥ
english: All of them wielded rocks as weapons; all hurled trees; all were armed with claws and fangs; and all were skilled in every kind of missile.

sanskrit: vicālayeyuḥ śailendrān bhedayeyuḥ sthirān drumān kṣobhayeyuś ca vegena samudraṃ saritāṃ patim
english: They could dislodge the greatest mountains, shatter firmly rooted trees, and with their speed churn the ocean, lord of rivers.

sanskrit: dārayeyuḥ kṣitiṃ padbhyām āplaveyur mahārṇavam nabhastalaṃ viśeyuś ca gṛhṇīyur api toyadān
english: They could split the earth with their feet, leap across the great ocean, soar through the vault of heaven, and seize the very clouds.

sanskrit: gṛhṇīyur api mātaṅgān mattān pravrajato vane nardamānāṃś ca nādena pātayeyur vihaṃgamān
english: They could seize rut-maddened elephants roaming the forest, and bring birds plummeting down from the sky with their roar.

sanskrit: īdṛśānāṃ prasūtāni harīṇāṃ kāmarūpiṇām śataṃ śatasahasrāṇi yūthapānāṃ mahātmanām babhūvur yūthapaśreṣṭhā vīrāṃś cājanayan harīn
english: Of such monkeys of every form, hundreds upon hundreds of thousands were born — great-souled troop-leaders — and the foremost among those troops in turn begot further valiant monkeys.

sanskrit: anye ṛkṣavataḥ prasthān upatasthuḥ sahasraśaḥ anye nānāvidhāñ śailān kānanāni ca bhejire
english: Some by the thousands took up positions on the slopes of Mount Ṛkṣavān; others spread across many different mountains and forests.

sanskrit: sūryaputraṃ ca sugrīvaṃ śakraputraṃ ca vālinam bhrātarāv upatasthus te sarva eva harīśvarāḥ
english: All those monkey-lords attended upon the two brothers: Sugrīva, son of the Sun, and Vālin, son of Indra.

sanskrit: tair meghavṛndācalakūṭakalpair mahābalair vānarayūthapālaiḥ babhūva bhūr bhīmaśarīrarūpaiḥ samāvṛtā rāmasahāyahetoḥ
english: By those mighty monkey-troop leaders — resembling clusters of storm-clouds and mountain peaks, formidable in body and form — the earth was covered over, for the sake of aiding Rāma.

sanskrit: nirvṛtte tu kratau tasmin hayamedhe mahātmanaḥ pratigṛhya surā bhāgān pratijagmur yathāgatam
english: When that horse-sacrifice of the great-souled king was concluded, the gods received their respective portions and departed the way they had come.

sanskrit: samāptadīkṣāniyamaḥ patnīgaṇasamanvitaḥ praviveśa purīṃ rājā sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ
english: The king, his vows of consecration fulfilled, accompanied by his group of queens, together with his ministers, army, and retinue, re-entered his city.

sanskrit: yathārhaṃ pūjitās tena rājñā vai pṛthivīśvarāḥ muditāḥ prayayur deśān praṇamya munipuṃgavam
english: Honoured fittingly by that king, the lords of the earth departed joyfully to their own realms, after bowing to the foremost of sages.

sanskrit: gateṣu pṛthivīśeṣu rājā daśarathaḥ punaḥ praviveśa purīṃ śrīmān puraskṛtya dvijottamān
english: Once the lords of the earth had gone, the illustrious King Daśaratha re-entered his city with the foremost of Brāhmaṇas leading the way.

sanskrit: śāntayā prayayau sārdham ṛśyaśṛṅgaḥ supūjitaḥ anvīyamāno rājñātha sānuyātreṇa dhīmatā
english: Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, greatly honoured, departed together with Śāntā, followed by the wise king and his entire retinue.

sanskrit: kausalyājanayad rāmaṃ divyalakṣaṇasaṃyutam viṣṇor ardhaṃ mahābhāgaṃ putram ikṣvākunandanam
english: Kausalyā gave birth to Rāma, endowed with divine marks, bearing half of Viṣṇu's essence, supremely blessed, the joy of the Ikṣvāku lineage.

sanskrit: kausalyā śuśubhe tena putreṇāmitatejasā yathā vareṇa devānām aditir vajrapāṇinā
english: Kausalyā shone with that son of boundless radiance as Aditi of the gods shines with Indra the Thunderbolt-bearer.

sanskrit: bharato nāma kaikeyyāṃ jajñe satyaparākramaḥ sākṣād viṣṇoś caturbhāgaḥ sarvaiḥ samudito guṇaiḥ
english: To Kaikeyī was born one named Bharata, true in valour — a direct fourth part of Viṣṇu, praised for all his virtues.

sanskrit: atha lakṣmaṇaśatrughnau sumitrājanayat sutau vīrau sarvāstrakuśalau viṣṇor ardhasamanvitau
english: Then Sumitrā bore two sons, Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna — heroes skilled in all weapons, jointly possessing a half portion of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: rājñaḥ putrā mahātmānaś catvāro jajñire pṛthak guṇavanto 'nurūpāś ca rucyā proṣṭhapadopamāḥ
english: Four great-souled sons were born to the king, each separately, virtuous and fitting, brilliant as stars in the month of Proṣṭhapada.

sanskrit: atītyaikādaśāhaṃ tu nāma karma tathākarot jyeṣṭhaṃ rāmaṃ mahātmānaṃ bharataṃ kaikayīsutam
english: Eleven days having passed, he performed the naming rite accordingly: the eldest — the great-souled Rāma; and Bharata, son of Kaikeyī;

sanskrit: saumitriṃ lakṣmaṇam iti śatrughnam aparaṃ tathā vasiṣṭhaḥ paramaprīto nāmāni kṛtavāṃs tadā teṣāṃ janmakriyādīni sarvakarmāṇy akārayat
english: Saumitri as Lakṣmaṇa, and the other as Śatrughna — so Vasiṣṭha, deeply pleased, assigned these names. He also performed all the birth-rites and ceremonies for them from the beginning.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ ketur iva jyeṣṭho rāmo ratikaraḥ pituḥ babhūva bhūyo bhūtānāṃ svayambhūr iva saṃmataḥ
english: Among them, the eldest, Rāma, was like a banner — a source of delight to his father — esteemed even more by all beings as Svayambhū himself is esteemed.

sanskrit: sarve vedavidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve lokahite ratāḥ sarve jñānopasaṃpannāḥ sarve samuditā guṇaiḥ
english: All were learned in the Vedas, all were heroes, all were devoted to the welfare of the world, all were endowed with wisdom, all were filled with virtues.

sanskrit: teṣām api mahātejā rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ bālyāt prabhṛti susnigdho lakṣmaṇo lakṣmivardhanaḥ
english: Among them, Lakṣmaṇa, the increaser of fortune, the greatly radiant Rāma of true valour — Lakṣmaṇa was deeply devoted to him from childhood onward.

sanskrit: rāmasya lokarāmasya bhrātur jyeṣṭhasya nityaśaḥ sarvapriyakaras tasya rāmasyāpi śarīrataḥ
english: He was ever doing everything agreeable to his eldest brother Rāma, the delight of the world — even as though he were another of Rāma's own bodies.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇo lakṣmisaṃpanno bahiḥprāṇa ivāparaḥ na ca tena vinā nidrāṃ labhate puruṣottamaḥ mṛṣṭam annam upānītam aśnāti na hi taṃ vinā
english: Lakṣmaṇa, endowed with auspiciousness, was like an external life-breath to that best of men. Without him, Rāma could not sleep; nor would he eat pure food brought before him without Lakṣmaṇa present.

sanskrit: yadā hi hayam ārūḍho mṛgayāṃ yāti rāghavaḥ tadainaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'bhyeti sadhanuḥ paripālayan
english: Whenever the Rāghava mounted his horse and went hunting, Lakṣmaṇa would follow behind him, bow in hand, protecting him.

sanskrit: bharatasyāpi śatrughno lakṣmaṇāvarajo hi saḥ prāṇaiḥ priyataro nityaṃ tasya cāsīt tathā priyaḥ
english: Śatrughna too — the younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa — was always dearer to Bharata than life itself, and was equally beloved by Bharata.

sanskrit: sa caturbhir mahābhāgaiḥ putrair daśarathaḥ priyaiḥ babhūva paramaprīto devair iva pitāmahaḥ
english: Daśaratha with his four greatly blessed and beloved sons was supremely joyful, as Pitāmaha is joyful with the gods.

sanskrit: te yadā jñānasaṃpannāḥ sarve samuditā guṇaiḥ hrīmantaḥ kīrtimantaś ca sarvajñā dīrghadarśinaḥ
english: When they became endowed with knowledge, filled with virtues, modest, illustrious, all-knowing, and far-sighted —

sanskrit: atha rājā daśarathas teṣāṃ dārakriyāṃ prati cintayām āsa dharmātmā sopādhyāyaḥ sabāndhavaḥ
english: — then the righteous-souled King Daśaratha, together with his preceptors and kinsmen, began to think about their marriages.

sanskrit: tasya cintayamānasya mantrimadhye mahātmanaḥ abhyāgacchan mahātejo viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
english: While that great-souled king was deliberating in the midst of his counsellors, the greatly radiant great sage Viśvāmitra arrived.

sanskrit: sa rājño darśanākāṅkṣī dvārādhyakṣān uvāca ha śīghram ākhyāta māṃ prāptaṃ kauśikaṃ gādhinaḥ sutam
english: Desiring audience with the king, he spoke to the gatekeepers: "Announce quickly that the son of Gādhi, Kauśika, has arrived."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya rājaveśma pradudruvuḥ saṃbhrāntamanasaḥ sarve tena vākyena coditāḥ
english: Hearing those words of his, all of them, their minds agitated, ran quickly to the royal palace, urged on by that command.

sanskrit: te gatvā rājabhavanaṃ viśvāmitram ṛṣiṃ tadā prāptam āvedayām āsur nṛpāyekṣvākave tadā
english: Going to the royal palace, they then announced to King Ikṣvāku — to Daśaratha — that the sage Viśvāmitra had arrived.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā sapurodhāḥ samāhitaḥ pratyujjagāma saṃhṛṣṭo brahmāṇam iva vāsavaḥ
english: Hearing those words of theirs, the king, composing himself, went out with his chaplain to meet him, rejoicing as Vāsava goes to meet Brahmā.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā jvalitaṃ dīptyā tāpasaṃ saṃśitavratam prahṛṣṭavadano rājā tato 'rghyam upahārayat
english: Seeing the ascetic blazing with lustre and firm in his vows, the king with a delighted countenance then presented the arghya offering.

sanskrit: sa rājñaḥ pratigṛhyārghyaṃ śāstradṛṣṭtena karmaṇā kuśalaṃ cāvyayaṃ caiva paryapṛcchan narādhipam
english: He received the arghya from the king according to the rite prescribed by scripture, and then enquired of the lord of men about his well-being and about the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaṃ ca samāgamya kuśalaṃ munipuṃgavaḥ ṛṣīṃś ca tān yathā nyāyaṃ mahābhāgān uvāca ha
english: Meeting Vasiṣṭha, that foremost of sages duly enquired about his welfare, and then addressed in proper order those greatly blessed sages present.

sanskrit: te sarve hṛṣṭamanasas tasya rājño niveśanam viviśuḥ pūjitās tatra niṣeduś ca yathārthataḥ
english: All of them, with gladdened hearts, entered that king's dwelling; honoured therein, they took their seats according to rank.

sanskrit: atha hṛṣṭamanā rājā viśvāmitraṃ mahāmunim uvāca paramodāro hṛṣṭas tam abhipūjayan
english: Then the king, his mind rejoicing, spoke to the great sage Viśvāmitra — supremely generous, joyful, honouring him:

sanskrit: yathāmṛtasya saṃprāptir yathā varṣam anūdake yathā sadṛśadāreṣu putrajanmāprajasya ca pranaṣṭasya yathā lābho yathā harṣo mahodaye tathaivāgamanaṃ manye svāgataṃ te mahāmune
english: "As is the attainment of ambrosia, as is rain upon a waterless land, as is the birth of a son to one who is childless and has a befitting wife, as is the recovery of what was lost, as is joy at a great occasion of rising — even so do I regard your arrival. Welcome, O great sage.

sanskrit: kaṃ ca te paramaṃ kāmaṃ karomi kim u harṣitaḥ pātrabhūto 'si me vipra diṣṭyā prāpto 'si dhārmika adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ ca sujīvitam
english: What supreme wish shall I fulfil for you? What does your joy require? You are a worthy vessel for me, O Brāhmaṇa; by good fortune have you come, O righteous one. Today my birth is fruitful and my life truly well-lived.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ rājarṣiśabdena tapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ brahmarṣitvam anuprāptaḥ pūjyo 'si bahudhā mayā
english: You who once shone by the title of royal sage, and whose lustre was illumined by austerity, have now attained the status of a brahmarṣi — you are worthy of my homage in many ways.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam idaṃ vipra pavitraṃ paramaṃ mama śubhakṣetragataś cāhaṃ tava saṃdarśanāt prabho
english: This, O Brāhmaṇa, is wondrous and supremely purifying for me; in beholding you, O Lord, I have entered upon auspicious ground.

sanskrit: brūhi yat prārthitaṃ tubhyaṃ kāryam āgamanaṃ prati icchāmy anugṛhīto 'haṃ tvadarthaparivṛddhaye
english: Tell me what you desire and what business has brought you here. I wish to be graced by accomplishing that which is for your sake and advancement.

sanskrit: kāryasya na vimarśaṃ ca gantum arhasi kauśika kartā cāham aśeṣeṇa daivataṃ hi bhavān mama
english: And you should not depart without deliberating on the matter, O Kauśika; I will carry out everything completely, for you are my very deity.

sanskrit: iti hṛdayasukhaṃ niśamya vākyaṃ śrutisukham ātmavatā vinītam uktam prathitaguṇayaśā guṇair viśiṣṭaḥ parama ṛṣiḥ paramaṃ jagāma harṣam
english: Hearing those words — pleasing to the heart and the ear, spoken with humility by a man of self-mastery — that foremost of sages, whose virtues and fame were widely celebrated and who was distinguished by his qualities, attained supreme delight.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā rājasiṃhasya vākyam adbhutavistaram hṛṣṭaromā mahātejā viśvāmitro 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Having heard the wondrous and far-ranging words of that lion among kings, the greatly radiant Viśvāmitra, his body-hairs erect with joy, spoke:

sanskrit: sadṛśaṃ rājaśārdūla tavaitad bhuvi nānyataḥ mahāvaṃśaprasūtasya vasiṣṭhavyapadeśinaḥ
english: "This is fitting for you, O tiger among kings, and for none else on earth — born of a great lineage and guided by the preceptorship of Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: yat tu me hṛdgataṃ vākyaṃ tasya kāryasya niścayam kuruṣva rājaśārdūla bhava satyapratiśravaḥ
english: The matter that lies in my heart — fulfil the resolve of that business, O tiger among kings; be one whose promise is true.

sanskrit: ahaṃ niyamam ātiṣṭha siddhyarthaṃ puruṣarṣabha tasya vighnakarau dvau tu rākṣasau kāmarūpiṇau
english: I am undertaking a vow for the sake of its accomplishment, O bull among men; but two rākṣasas who can change form at will are obstructors of it.

sanskrit: vrate me bahuśaś cīrṇe samāptyāṃ rākṣasāv imau mārīcaś ca subāhuś ca vīryavantau suśikṣitau tau māṃsarudhiraugheṇa vediṃ tām abhyavarṣatām
english: Even when my vow has been long observed and is near completion, these two rākṣasas — Mārīca and Subāhu, powerful and well-trained — defile that altar with torrents of flesh and blood.

sanskrit: avadhūte tathā bhūte tasmin niyamaniścaye kṛtaśramo nirutsāhas tasmād deśād apākrame
english: When that firm vow is thus violated and overthrown, I — exhausted in effort and disheartened — withdraw from that place.

sanskrit: na ca me krodham utsraṣṭuṃ buddhir bhavati pārthiva tathābhūtā hi sā caryā na śāpas tatra mucyate
english: And it does not accord with my intention to release a curse in anger, O king; for such is the nature of that observance — no curse may be uttered there.

sanskrit: svaputraṃ rājaśārdūla rāmaṃ satyaparākramam kākapakṣadharaṃ śūraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ me dātum arhasi
english: You ought to give me, O tiger among kings, your own son — Rāma of true valour, the hero who still wears the side-locks of boyhood, your eldest.

sanskrit: śakto hy eṣa mayā gupto divyena svena tejasā rākṣasā ye vikartāras teṣām api vināśane
english: For he, protected by me and by his own divine radiance, is capable of destroying those rākṣasas who are the perpetrators of that desecration.

sanskrit: śreyaś cāsmai pradāsyāmi bahurūpaṃ na saṃśayaḥ trayāṇām api lokānāṃ yena khyātiṃ gamiṣyati
english: And I will bestow upon him manifold blessings, of no doubt, by which he will win renown across all three worlds.

sanskrit: na ca tau rāmam āsādya śaktau sthātuṃ kathaṃ cana na ca tau rāghavād anyo hantum utsahate pumān
english: Those two will not be able to stand in any way once they encounter Rāma; nor is there any man other than that Rāghava who would dare to slay them.

sanskrit: vīryotsiktau hi tau pāpau kālapāśavaśaṃ gatau rāmasya rājaśārdūla na paryāptau mahātmanaḥ
english: Those two wicked ones, intoxicated with their own power, are already in the grip of the noose of time; O tiger among kings, they are no match whatsoever for the great-souled Rāma.

sanskrit: na ca putrakṛtaṃ snehaṃ kartum arhasi pārthiva ahaṃ te pratijānāmi hatau tau viddhi rākṣasau
english: You ought not to act out of paternal affection for your son, O king. I give you my solemn promise: know those two rākṣasas as already slain.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vedmi mahātmānaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākramam vasiṣṭho 'pi mahātejā ye ceme tapasi sthitāḥ
english: I know the great-souled Rāma of true valour, and so does the greatly radiant Vasiṣṭha, and all these others who are established in austerity.

sanskrit: yadi te dharmalābhaṃ ca yaśaś ca paramaṃ bhuvi sthiram icchasi rājendra rāmaṃ me dātum arhasi
english: If you desire the attainment of dharma and supreme and lasting fame in this world, O lord of kings, you ought to give Rāma to me.

sanskrit: yady abhyanujñāṃ kākutstha dadate tava mantriṇaḥ vasiṣṭha pramukhāḥ sarve tato rāmaṃ visarjaya
english: If your ministers, headed by Vasiṣṭha, all give their assent, O Kākutstha, then send Rāma forth.

sanskrit: abhipretam asaṃsaktam ātmajaṃ dātum arhasi daśarātraṃ hi yajñasya rāmaṃ rājīvalocanam
english: You ought to give willingly and without attachment your own son — lotus-eyed Rāma — for ten nights, the duration of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: nātyeti kālo yajñasya yathāyaṃ mama rāghava tathā kuruṣva bhadraṃ te mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: The time of the sacrifice will not pass beyond its due limit, O Rāghava; act accordingly — may it go well with you — and do not give your mind over to grief.

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā dharmātmā dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ virarāma mahātejā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
english: Having thus spoken these words in accord with dharma and its purpose, the greatly radiant great sage Viśvāmitra, righteous in soul, fell silent.

sanskrit: iti hṛdayamanovidāraṇaṃ munivacanaṃ tad atīva śuśruvān narapatir agamad bhayaṃ mahad vyathitamanāḥ pracacāla cāsanāt
english: Having thus heard those words of the sage — which rent his heart and mind — the lord of men was seized with great fear; his mind distressed, he trembled upon his seat.
